newsitem.title: UK: Wickes to cut 51 mln from shareholders funds.
newsitem.headline: Wickes to cut 51 mln from shareholders funds.

text.p: Home improvement retailer Wickes Plc said it will take a 51 million stg reduction in consolidated shareholders funds for 1995 as part of the restating its 1995 accounts.
The company said its former chairman and chief executive Henry Sweetbaum has accepted "ultimate responsibility" for overstating profits and would be repaying 1.2 million stg in bonus payments.
The restatement of the accounts will result in a reduction of 26 million stg in operating profit for 1995, 14 million for 1994 and 11 million for earlier years.
Wickes said the adjustments were provisional as further minor revisions might be necessary.
The group said its shareholders funds will have to be cut by a further two million stg to cover similar rebate issues in its continental European business.
Wickes will also need to make a 10 million stg property provision for exposure to property leases and unoccupied freeholds but this is not linked to accounting irregularities.
The impact of Wickes accounting irregularities were explained by chairman Michael von Brentano in a letter to shareholders.
A full report by solicitors Linklaters & Paines and accountants Price Waterhouse confirmed there was "serious mismanagement in relation to certain important areas of the group's operations", it said.
This was principally in the buying department where there was "a deliberate misrepresentation of the true basis of certain rebate and contribution arrangements with suppliers."

Former finance director Trefor Llewellyn has agreed to repay his 485,000 stg bonus for 1995. He has denied any knowledge of the nature of the rebate arrangements in the buying departrment which led to the accounting irregularities.

The company said disciplinary proceedings have been taken against two Wickes directors with responsibility for the buying department. Disciplinary proceedings involving further middle ranking executives and more junior employees would be implemented in due course, it said.
Wickes said it expects to bolster its finances via a rights issue and bank loans as soon as possible, but the amounts have yet to be determined.
"The board intends to seek sufficient new equity to reduce the group's gearing to a more acceptable level.
The group said it would not seek to have its share suspension lifted until new shares under the rights offering are issued. It will publish a prospectus for the issue in December.
